idiom_name: hand-written struct + designated initializer, passed by const pointer
implementation_notes: C has the value type but none of the generated machinery: declare a struct whose members are the former parameters, give it a designated initializer (C99) or an initialization function, and pass a `const struct ... *` so callers read names instead of positions and large groups are not copied. There is no constructor, default-argument or equality support, so defaults live in an init helper and comparisons are written by hand - the hand-written struct plus that helper is both the idiomatic and the only available form. A struct passed by value is still fine for a tiny group that never changes shape.
pitfalls: A struct passed by value copies every member; for anything but a tiny group pass `const struct *` and document that the callee must not keep the pointer.
Positional (non-designated) initializers silently shift meaning when a member is inserted - keep designators or an init helper.
Growing the struct changes its size and ABI, so a carrier that crosses a module or shared-library boundary must be rebuilt together or versioned.
